column1: # Tool-usage rules. One per line, tab-separated:
#   id <TAB> ERE matched against the Bash command <TAB> message <TAB> incident
# THE BAR: a rule belongs here only if the idiom fails SILENTLY — it hands back
# a confident wrong answer rather than an error. Anything that errors out is
# already self-announcing and must not be added; a rule that fires on healthy
# commands trains dismissal and is worse than no rule at all.
# Never append blindly: a lesson that is a special case of a rule here EXTENDS
# that rule rather than growing a sibling. Fusion is the whole anti-bloat
# discipline. A pattern is inadmissible until it is shown to catch the bad
# command AND leave a healthy one alone.

column3: Piping into head/tail makes `$?` the exit code of HEAD, not of your command — a failing grep reads as success. Capture the status before piping, or drop the pipe.
column4: 2026-08-21 `grep -rw AppearanceCubit lib --include=*.dart | head -3; echo "exit=$?"` printed exit=0 for a symbol that does not exist anywhere.

column3: No UTF-8 locale on this machine: `wc -m` and `cut -c` count BYTES. CJK is miscounted and truncation splits characters mid-sequence.
column4: 2026-08-21 `cut -c1-120` split multi-byte characters in CJK report lines; ugrep also aborted on a CJK pattern.

column3: `dart format` on a directory reformats untouched siblings and buries the real change in the diff. Format only the files this turn edited.

column3: A path beginning with '-' (every ~/.claude/projects/ folder does) is parsed as a FLAG by grep/ls/stat/cat; with stderr silenced it returns 0 matches and reads as 'nothing found'. Prefix ./ or put -- before it.
column4: Path starting with '-' is parsed as a flag by grep/ls/stat; with stderr silenced it reads as 'nothing found'
